items.title: What Star Wars got right about AI
items.summary_original: Two science-fiction futures for machine intelligence: the lonely oracle and the crowded junkyard. Only one of them came true. AI assisted. Droids are cheap, specialized, everywhere, and slightly annoying. That commodity vision maps to how artificial intelligence is reaching your desk right now. Science fiction gave us two competing pictures of artificial intelligence, and for decades we bet on the wrong one. Star Trek imagined a single, calm, all-knowing computer; one brain per starship, summoned by voice, answering anything. items.summary_original: SHIJI COMMONS transforms two stone houses into community hub Located in Hengshiji Village, Sanzao Town, Zhuhai, China , SHIJI COMMONS by StudioTiltedCircle transforms two traditional stone houses into a contemporary community space. Situated between the village fabric and the surrounding landscape, the project explores how an existing rural structure can be renewed while preserving its material memory and cultural identity. Rather than replacing the old, the project begins with the existing stone walls. Through dismantling, reclaiming, and reusing the original stone, the material is transformed from a structural element into a new spatial interface. items.title: OODA designs DUAS towers as a pair of marble figures gazing over albania’s coast
items.summary_original: a pair of towers between the mountains and the adriatic Along Albania ’s southern coast, OODA has designed DUAS Towers as a pair of 98-meter mixed-use buildings rising above Vlorë, a city which sits between the mountains and the Adriatic Sea. One tower is circular and the other quadrangular, yet both follow the same architectural system. A horizontal volume forms the base, an upright slab rises through the center, and another horizontal piece closes the composition overhead. Their name follows the pairing too. Duas is Portuguese for two. The difference between the two appears most clearly from a distance. The rectangular tower measures 30 by 25 meters, while its neighbor forms a 26-meter-wide circle. Ein Turm ist kreisförmig und der andere viereckig, doch beide folgen demselben architektonischen System. Ein horizontales Volumen bildet die Basis, eine aufrechte Platte erhebt sich durch die Mitte und ein weiteres horizontales Stück schließt die Komposition über dem Kopf ab. items.title: Is there a retirement crisis in the creative industry?
items.summary_original: Retirement plans are changing for creatives. Image licensed via Adobe Stock Right now, senior creatives are planning to exit the industry much earlier than expected. So what exactly is going on? There's a conversation in creative industries right now that's largely going under the radar. It's happening in DMs, in whispered conversations at industry events, and at 3am when people can't sleep. The conversation starts with this: "I think I need to retire." Take illustrator and designer Jason Roberts . "I've gone from thinking 'I might never retire' to 'I might have to retire early' in a pretty short space of time," he admits. items.title_de: Gibt es in der Kreativbranche eine Ruhestandskrise?
items.summary_de: Die Ruhestandspläne für Kreative ändern sich. Bild lizenziert über Adobe Stock Derzeit planen erfahrene Kreative, die Branche viel früher als erwartet zu verlassen. Was genau ist also los? In der Kreativbranche gibt es derzeit eine Diskussion, die weitgehend unter dem Radar bleibt. Es passiert in Direktnachrichten, in geflüsterten Gesprächen bei Branchenveranstaltungen und um 3 Uhr morgens, wenn die Leute nicht schlafen können. Das Gespräch beginnt damit: „Ich glaube, ich muss in den Ruhestand gehen.“ Nehmen Sie den Illustrator und Designer Jason Roberts. „Ich bin innerhalb kürzester Zeit von dem Gedanken ‚Ich werde vielleicht nie in Rente gehen‘ zu ‚Ich muss vielleicht früher in Rente gehen‘ übergegangen“, gibt er zu. „Ich dachte wirklich, dass ich nie genug verdienen würde, um wirklich in Rente zu gehen. Aber wenn KI mich aus meiner eigenen Branche verdrängen würde, müsste ich vielleicht früher in den Ruhestand gehen, einen Weg finden, über die Runden zu kommen, oder vielleicht meine Arbeit verkaufen.“

But her architect's eye never left her, as it runs under everything from her award-winning Barron's covers to a quirky garden of plants that don't exist. Carolina Moscoso never set out to be an illustrator. Yet the New York-based Portuguese artist has spent the last few years working for the likes of Barron's, Bloomberg Markets, Politico and the Washington Post – even winning an award along the way. She turns some of the driest, most technical briefs into thought-provoking images you could hang on your wall, which is her speciality. items.summary_original: Ferro is a type family that turns information loss into a design principle, bridging Renaissance metal type and the early computer age. It began as a display face for CodeX, an editorial project on digital cultures whose second issue, designed by the collective Bonjour Monde , explored media archaeology and the French Minitel, asking how medium-specific works can survive once the technologies that produced them disappear.wide Its source is the Annales Suevici, printed in 1595, whose roman, italic, and blackletter Ferro reinterprets rather than restores. Centered on a vibrant red color palette, the project explores four craft traditions: bamboo fencing, kumihimo braided cord, washi paper , and urushi lacquer, through furniture , lighting , and storage objects. The collection considers how traditional materials and production methods can be integrated into familiar domestic settings while retaining their craft characteristics. Das Projekt konzentriert sich auf eine leuchtend rote Farbpalette und erforscht vier Handwerkstraditionen: Bambuszäune, geflochtene Kumihimo-Schnüre, Washi-Papier und Urushi-Lack, durch Möbel, Beleuchtung und Aufbewahrungsobjekte. Die Sammlung befasst sich mit der Frage, wie traditionelle Materialien und Produktionsmethoden in vertraute häusliche Umgebungen integriert werden können und gleichzeitig ihre handwerklichen Eigenschaften beibehalten. Jedes Stück kombiniert funktionale Verwendung mit sichtbaren Bezügen zu seinem Material und Herstellungsprozess und schafft so eine Verbindung zwischen traditionellen japanischen Techniken

items.summary_original: Now, if you want to, you can use Google's 3D emoji in your own creations. The company shared some details about how it went about designing the little pictograms and why, as part of World Emoji Day on Friday. Things you might not necessarily worry about in a 2D illustration suddenly become very important when you're talking about a 3D model. Is a smiley face a sphere? A mask? A flat disc? items.title: How Baseline Can Help You Ship Less JavaScript
items.summary_original: Most of us install a dependency once and never look at it again. It does its job, the tests pass, and we move on. But the web platform keeps moving too, and a surprising number of the libraries sitting in your package.json today are now built into the browser. In a typical mid-sized JavaScript app, you can often find somewhere between 60KB and 90KB (minified and gzipped) of dependencies that the platform can now handle on its own. Date and number formatting, HTTP requests, modals, tooltips, deep cloning, grouping arrays: these were all real gaps a few years ago. A lot of them aren’t gaps anymore. items.title: ‘play is itself a function’: luca boscardin on designing toys, cities, and spaces for imagination
items.summary_original: luca boscardin discusses how play shapes cities and learning Luca Boscardin doesn’t believe play belongs only to childhood. Across toys, playgrounds, books, and public installations, his work explores play as a way of thinking that invites curiosity. Whether through Archiville, a cardboard city with no instructions, or Animal Factory, his growing family of abstract animal structures produced by Magis , Boscardin creates open-ended objects that leave room for interpretation. After studying architecture in Venice before moving into graphic design, Boscardin gradually realized that what interested him was creating the conditions for imagination to flourish. Today, alongside his work as a designer, illustrator, and educator, he collaborates with institutions including Palazzo Grassi , La Trien

items.summary_original: Gabled Timber Volume Opens Toward Pine Landscape A&A House is set within a mature pine grove in a small town in Poland , where the existing trees and natural topography became the starting point for the design by Rasztawicki Bielinski Architects. Rather than clearing the site to accommodate the building, the house was positioned around the existing woodland, preserving its character and allowing the garden to merge naturally with the surrounding landscape. The architecture takes its cues from the familiar silhouette of a traditional barn , reinterpreted through a restrained contemporary approach. Als Designforschungsprojekt entwickelt, untersucht es anhand des Igels als Flaggschiffart, wie fragmentierte städtische Lebensräume durch Landschaftseingriffe wieder verbunden werden können. Das Projekt schlägt ein miteinander verbundenes Netzwerk aus Lebensräumen, ökologischen Korridoren, Gärten und Lernräumen im Freien vor und verwandelt ungenutzte Stadtlandschaften in Umgebungen, die sowohl die Tierwelt als auch das alltägliche öffentliche Leben unterstützen. Anstatt die ökologische Infrastruktur von menschlicher Aktivität zu trennen, bringt der Vorschlag beides durch Bepflanzung, Wasser usw. zusammen

items.title: Schon mal so eine schicke Kampagne für einen Fußballverein gesehen?

Der Wiener Sport-Club ist Kult. Was alleine schon für einen schicken, kurzen Namen einer der ältesten Sportvereine Österreichs trägt. Bereits 1883 wurde er gegründet und ist, neben manchem fußballerischen Erfolg, auch bekannt für seine Tribüne, die an einen Friedhof grenzt – und für seine toleranten Fans . Die neue Saison hat er mit einem 2:0 gegen den Favoritner AC eingeläutet – und mit einer Kampagne von Karl Anders . items.title: Numa Is a Conceptual Cold Brew Built on Color and Pattern
items.summary_original: Ready to drink cold brew tends to split between moody minimal cans and overly illustrated cartons, but Numa skips both. Erika Luisetta built the entire system on horizontal color bands and a repeating geometric pattern, giving each flavor its own distinct palette and letting color alone signal Mocha from Matcha from Vanilla, all without a single illustrated bean or fruit in sight. The post Numa Is a Conceptual Cold Brew Built on Color and Pattern appeared first on DIELINE .
items.title_de: Numa ist ein konzeptionelles Kaltgetränk, das auf Farbe und Muster basiert
items.summary_de: Bei trinkfertigem Kaltgebräu gibt es tendenziell eine Aufspaltung zwischen stimmungsvollen Minimaldosen und übermäßig illustrierten Kartons, aber Numa verzichtet auf beides. Erika Luisetta baute das gesamte System auf horizontalen Farbbändern und einem sich wiederholenden geometrischen Muster auf, um jeder Geschmacksrichtung eine eigene, unverwechselbare Palette zu verleihen und die Farbe allein Mokka, Matcha und Vanille signalisieren zu lassen, ohne dass eine einzige abgebildete Bohne oder Frucht in Sicht war. Der Beitrag „Numa ist ein konzeptionelles Cold Brew, das auf Farbe und Muster basiert“ erschien zuerst auf DIELINE.
